notes.text: Mathew Barzal is out (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matias Maccelli is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games.
Ryan Pulock is out 2-4 weeks (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Tony DeAngelo has taken his spot beside Adam Pelech.
Ben Hutton was added to the roster on Nov 6.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, down from 37% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 22% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:38 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Alexander Wennberg has not dressed for the last 10 games. He is a top-six forward.
Alexander Wennberg is expected back after missing 10 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Filip Bystedt was added to the roster on Oct 29 and has played beside Tyler Toffoli and Ivar Stenberg.
Eric Pohlkamp was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Dmitry Orlov.

SJS.head: Close, but the Islanders have the slight edge
SJS.body: The Islanders have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but San Jose has home-ice advantage, and the Islanders will be without Barzal. The Sharks’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.

NYI.head: The Islanders have a slight edge

story.head: The Sharks need a win
paras: The Sharks are on a five-game losing streak, and the Islanders are winless in three (0-2-1). Going in, the Islanders are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Sharks sixth in the Pacific (26th).

The Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). They also roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd), so the Isles roll four lines, but the Sharks lean on their top six. The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (4th lowest), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (30th). San Jose has scored 2.47 goals a game, the third fewest in the league, and allowed 3.58, the fourth most. Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Bo Horvat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 16 GP) is tied for the Islanders’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 16 GP) shares it. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (7 G / 14 A / 21 P in 17 GP).
Ilya Sorokin (6-4-1 / .909 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for the Islanders, and Yaroslav Askarov (4-8-0 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) for San Jose.
